shared_elements: upright anthropomorphic/animal figures rendered as flat silhouettes
repeated figures aligned in a row/register
figures set directly on an unshaped natural stone surface
justification: Both surfaces carry small, highly schematic profile creatures and a disc-like motif arranged in loose rows on bare stone, and both are figural rather than purely ornamental, which is about as far as the correspondence goes. The decisive differences are technique and format: A is thin red pigment painted on a broad sloping natural outcrop with figures strung along one near-horizontal line, whereas B is deep carved relief on a shaped upright pillar with stacked registers separated by a band of repeated pattern.
